text:
Zoe: hey everyone, quick newbie question: my first oncall shift is next Wed night. what are the absolute must-dos before i take live pages?
Rafael: welcome! Must-dos: confirm PagerDuty device + MFA, runbook read-through for your services, and at least one staging shadow.
Kara: also verify you can access alerting dashboard (alerts.redwood) and the incident-playback logs. sometimes SSO needs a kick.
Zoe: i can open alerts.redwood but cannot see the service group for 'ingest'. PD shows 'No services'.
oncall-bot: reminder: complete PagerDuty device registration: https://pd.redwood/setup. If services missing, contact #eng-identity.
Rafael: PD mapping issue = usually missing team tags on your SSO profile. @Kara can confirm and add 'ingest-team' tag.
Kara: added the tag. give it 2 minutes then refresh. if still missing, open a ticket with screenshot.
Zoe: still empty after refresh. submitted a ticket to #eng-identity with emp id 8854.
Milo: while that's being fixed, you can shadow a staging drill to get comfortable. I run a short 'noisy-alert' sim Tue 17:00. join as observer.
Zoe: thanks, please add me. also, where are secure runbooks for key rotation kept?
Docs-Bot: secure-runbooks are under docs.internal/secure-runbooks. Request read access via the access form: https://forms.redwood/access.
Zoe: ok filed the access form. one more: if an alert looks like a spike but dash shows only a small blip, how do i decide to escalate?
Rafael: rule of thumb: if customer-visible errors or latency increase -> escalate immediately. If it's ambiguous, annotate with evidence (graphs + steps tried) and escalate after 10-15m if it doesn't trend down.
Kara: prefer early escalation. your timeline helps the next responder.
Zoe: what's the exact handoff we should use at shift change?
Milo: we use /handoff in #eng-oncall. short example you can copy:
```
/handoff
Shift: Zoe -> Rafael
Incidents: ingest-queue-lag (mitigated)
Status: replayed backlog, consumer restarted
Followups: investigate batching thresholds, ticket #5782
```
Zoe: helpful, thanks. any 'do not do' guidance for first-timers?
Rafael: don't rotate keys or change deployment configs alone unless paired. small fixes are ok but if it affects state, call for a second pair of eyes.
Kara: and don't mute alerts without opening a maintenance ticket. link the ticket to the suppression.
Zoe: got it. also, am i expected to run post-incident writeups?
Milo: for incidents you lead, create a short post-incident note on the board (template in pinned messages). assign an RCA owner if it's not you.
Docs-Bot: incident template: title, timeline, mitigation, followups, owner, and severity. Link: https://confluence.redwood/incident-template.
Zoe: last question: if pager chain doesn't acknowledge, what's the manual escalation?
Rafael: escalate up: oncall -> service owner -> oncall-lead. If unresolved for 15m and sev1, call the oncall-lead number and open a war-room channel, ping @exec-oncall.
Zoe: thanks all. i'll join Tue drill and follow up in the ticket once PD shows services. appreciate the help :slightly_smiling_face:
Milo: welcome! i'll pair with you on an early shift once PD is sorted.
oncall-bot: scheduled: staging-drill Tue 17:00 (invite sent).
Kara: ping me if you want a quick screenshare to walk through the alert dashboard before your shift.
Zoe: will do, thanks everyone :)
